eval.summary: AgentShield is a Node CLI that statically scans a .claude/ directory and grades it on secrets, permissions, hooks, MCP servers and agent prompts. It can run as a script you call on demand without taking over the runtime, so it passes the fit test as long as it's run from a pinned local build, not through the GitHub Action or GitHub App channels. Uncle J has red-team and blue-team skills but no mechanical scanner for its own hooks and MCP registrations, so this fills a real gap on accuracy and offline use. The adoption-eval method assumes a backend is being replaced; nothing is replaced here, so read this as an additive-tool judgment. The rule count and the breach statistics in the README are the author's own claims and haven't been verified.
eval.trial_sketch: Build a pinned copy in a throwaway directory with network disabled. Run `agentshield scan --path` with `--format json` against a copy of ~/.claude and the stack repo's mcp-clients config, never using --fix, --opus or --supply-chain-online. Hand-label each finding as true positive, false positive or noise, and record the runtime-confidence classification, wall-clock time and whether any network calls were attempted. Adopt only if real findings outnumber noise. If it's adopted, the JSON output would feed a refinery-doctor check at zero Claude tokens.

1155123554.note: Trial report-only, pinned version, never --fix: a static audit of ~/.claude settings/hooks/MCP/CLAUDE.md is a real gap. Queued for the scout rung-2 evaluation.

risks: Critical rules suppress the whole catalog, so one false positive on a first-party description (for example ask_local mentioning credential paths) could silently take a server's tools away

eval.summary: vex-mcp is a stdio proxy that sits in front of an MCP server's launch command. It checks tool catalogs for poisoning, hashes tool definitions to spot drift, and enforces allow and deny lists for each server. It also keeps a tamper-evident audit log. It fits as a wrapper without taking over the runtime: it is one config change per server, uses no model tokens, and its regex and Unicode checks should run fully offline once installed. Most of Uncle J's servers are first-party, so the main value is guarding the third-party servers started with `uvx`/`npx` (context7, duckdb, serena) and limiting write-capable tools. The regex detectors can wrongly suppress a whole catalog, and the stack upgrades often, so a trial should come before adopting it.
eval.trial_sketch: Put a pinned, locally installed copy (`cargo install` or `uv tool install`, not `npx @latest`) in front of context7, duckdb and one jcodemunch instance, using a throwaway project `.mcp.json` with the network off. Measure how many false flags or blocks the real tool catalogs trigger, how much drift noise comes after a jcodemunch or jdocmunch upgrade, the added round-trip time per tool call compared with the bench scripts, and whether a planted poisoned test server gets blocked. Token cost should stay at zero; check that blocked calls come back as short JSON-RPC errors and not long text.

1270868404.note: 2 stars and no push since 2026-06, sitting in every MCP call path: too much trust for too little track record. Regex catalog checks would also flag first-party servers.

eval.summary: Vestigium is a local stdio MCP server. It parses a PDF once with Docling, with OCR for scans, builds a BM25 index with no embeddings and no model calls, and lets the agent read by address (sections, pages, tables, notes) with a PDF page attached to every passage. That fills a real gap: Uncle J has no PDF route that passes the fit test, since markitdown is Microsoft and ruled out. It also matches Bill's goals in order: page-cited answers for accuracy, reading by address for token efficiency, and offline indexing. But the project is at 0.1.x, and every benchmark was run by the author, graded by an AI judge with no human check, and tested only in Claude Code. A throwaway trial should come before any routing change.
eval.trial_sketch: Install it into a separate venv with VESTIGIUM_HOME pointing at a temp dir, and ingest 3–5 long PDFs Bill actually uses, including one scanned PDF. Network must be off during ingest and querying. Ask about 20 questions whose answers you've already checked by hand. Compare Vestigium with the whole text read through jdocmunch/Read: score accuracy and citation correctness yourself, not with an AI judge, and log tokens and time per answer from the session. Also check Docling's dependency tree (OCR backend, any onnxruntime pull) against the Microsoft rule before keeping it.

1429971301.note: PDF reading is a real gap: jdocmunch's PDF path needs the office extra (not installed here) and that pulls markitdown (Microsoft). Vestigium uses Docling instead. 13 stars and self-graded benchmarks, so it needs a trial on Bill's own PDFs. Queued for rung-2 evaluation.
